eventMetadata.context_description: **Marine layer moderation and onshore flow are anchoring trader expectations for a highest temperature near 80°F in Los Angeles on August 21.** National Weather Service point forecasts for KLAX indicate a high around 78–80°F under mostly sunny conditions, consistent with typical late-August coastal climatology where the average daily maximum sits near 84°F but frequently falls into the upper 70s when the marine layer persists or weak onshore winds develop. Recent observations show downtown and airport readings in the mid-80s on August 19–20, yet models suggest a slight cooling trend into the 21st as high pressure weakens and sea breezes strengthen, keeping peak values below heat-wave thresholds. This scientific consensus—supported by NWS guidance and ensemble agreement—directly underpins the market’s heavy weighting on the 78–81°F brackets (collectively ~77.5% implied probability), while low odds on 82°F+ reflect limited potential for significant inland heating or offshore flow tomorrow. Traders are effectively pricing the narrow forecast window between normal variability and any last-minute model shifts in boundary-layer moisture or wind patterns.
